name: Matcha

harvest.season: shaded first flush, stone-milled from tencha
harvest.pluckingStage: same shaded leaf as gyokuro, destemmed and degveined

processing.description: Like gyokuro, then dried without rolling — that unswept leaf is tencha.
Tencha ground to matcha. Ceremonial vs culinary is leaf grade plus mill freshness.

taste: usucha: frothy umami; koicha: dense sweet broth
profile.mouthfeel: suspension, not an infusion — the leaf is drunk

infusions.notes: Usucha: ~2 g / 70 ml, whisk into foam
Koicha: ~4 g / 30 ml, knead slowly, no foam
Whisk, do not steep and discard

water: Soft, ~75 °C. Sift the powder. Koicha wants even better leaf than usucha.
storage: Freezer, then fridge; small tins. Matcha dies in weeks once opened.
summary: Stone-milled shaded tencha: usucha froth and koicha paste are two ratios of the same powder.
